newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges, cargoes higher on low avails.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges, cargoes higher on low avails.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges moved higher late on Thursday on what traders said was a shortage in prompt material and higher swaps but some said they saw an attempt to push prices higher for pricing purposes.
High sulphur cargoes were also assessed higher with some buying interest seen while one percent was a touch stronger with few avails left after several buyers snatched up cargoes this week.
High sulphur barges traded twice at $89.25 fob Rotterdam and later at $89.50, up to $1.50 over Wednesday's close, after trading early in the day at $88.50.
Other trades were reported by mid-day at $87.50 for lower quality storage material, the traders added.
"There's not that much available and bunker demand is healthier," one trader said. Traders put total demand around the 20,000-tonne mark.
However some traders said some market players were trying to push up the market to affect the cargo quotes.

Low sulphur barges rose late in the day to $97.50 on the offer side on higher swaps but other sellers were at $1.50 lower, the level for most of the week. Buyers were early in the day at $94 but no deals were heard done.
One trader said demand might pick up next week as "some people may have to cover some short positions". A major sold some material at steady prices but the deal was private and confidential.

High sulphur cargoes were assessed stronger after swaps picked up and with some buying interest was seen. Some traders put cargoes around the $86 cif mark after a cargo changed hands late on Wednesday at high fob +$4, compared with $1.50 less for a deal on Tuesday.

"Crude is up so swaps followed...and a lot of the people in the market see that not that much is around. We have moved a lot of Russian material to the States. Stock levels are less," a trader, Wednesday's buyer, said.
Another trader was heard to be pricing a cargo to be taken out of the region while a utility short to be covered was seen as contributing to the absence of material, traders said.

One percent was a little higher with a cargo traded at the $94.50 fob level, picked up by a trader. After a flurry of activity this week, particularly by a Mediterranean buyer, one cargo was seen left on the market, traders said.
